coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
coursesExamined.contribution: Required personal/academic development, research literacy and civic engagement.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. coursesExamined.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
coursesExamined.contribution: Provides specific complementary financial-statement analysis,accountability,costing,budgeting,organisational control and investment appraisal using discounted cash flows. These support interpretation of company data andfinancial choices; they do not supply a quantitative-finance specialisation.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.

coursesExamined.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course includes a multi-faceted exploration of AI’s business, managerial, economic and related societal implications. Designed for students with a strong interest in AI, it requires no prior technical background.
coursesExamined.contribution: Studies AI foundations/limitations and business,economic andsocietal implications through cases andcountry-level AIreadiness/workforce/regulation inquiry. This supplies specific economic/application context for data-science decisions,not technical machine learning.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides the introductory microeconomic and macroeconomic framework needed for quantitative economic applications
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

coursesExamined.name: International Macroeconomics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops short/medium/long-run macroeconomic models,expectations,open-economy dynamics andfiscal/monetary policy using algebra,graphs andindicators. This supplies macroeconomic interpretation rather than a dedicated trade-theory sequence.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.

coursesExamined.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops advanced microeconomic analysis of uncertainty, strategic behaviour, market structure, equilibrium and efficiency
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.

coursesExamined.name: Public Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
coursesExamined.contribution: uses theoretical models and empirical evidence to analyse market failure, taxation, redistribution and public policy
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

coursesExamined.name: Econometrics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
coursesExamined.contribution: directly develops econometric estimation, testing, causal analysis, prediction and Monte Carlo simulation in Stata
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. coursesExamined.name: Research Methods & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides foundational research design, statistics and empirical-analysis skills for later econometric work
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

coursesExamined.name: AI Ethics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines AI through ethical theory and psychological accounts of human behaviour and interaction. Ethical debates address fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Psychological perspectives consider development, clinical care, social and organizational relationships, forensic applications and cognitive neuroscience. Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores philosophical foundations and implications of AI. Examines the history of AI, ethical issues like interpretability, bias and alignment, debates about AI consciousness and implications for human nature.
coursesExamined.contribution: adds explicit ethical analysis of algorithmic systems, including fairness, accountability, privacy and responsibility
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

coursesExamined.name: Decision-making in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops probabilistic inference,Bayesian networks,temporal models,decision theory,Markov decision processes,partial observability andbandits. This is actual mathematical decision-making under uncertainty; not a specialised logistics or stochastics course.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

coursesExamined.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces formal logic, abstract mathematical reasoning and proof. Students analyze propositions and quantified statements, work with sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, and develop direct and indirect proofs. Induction and recursive definitions extend these tools to mathematical structures. The final component systematically models processes and games without chance and investigates the existence and construction of winning strategies.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops propositional/predicate logic,sets,relations,proof,induction,recursion anddeterministic process/game reasoning. These mathematical foundations complement formal models andalgorithms; no full optimisation syllabus is inferred.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction.

coursesExamined.name: Optimization Methods in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies search and optimization for rational agents in known, complex and adversarial environments. Students move from uninformed and heuristic search to local and global optimization, first- and second-order methods and population approaches. Adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimization extend the toolkit. Laboratories and projects require algorithm tracing, implementation and evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Covers computational methods for search problems in complex and adversarial environments. Includes uninformed and informed search, local and global search, adversarial games and constraint satisfaction problems.
coursesExamined.contribution: Studies heuristic/global/local search,first/second-order methods,population approaches,constraint satisfaction,linear programming anddiscrete optimisation with implementation/evaluation. Actual optimisation methods contribute directly; dedicated convex/nonlinear-programming course equivalence is not claimed.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

coursesExamined.name: Software Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops software-construction skills through C++ and functional programming in Haskell, alongside software design and quality assurance. C++ work addresses classes, inheritance, polymorphism and memory management; Haskell introduces functions, recursion, types and input/output. Laboratories apply version control, code review, debugging, testing, documentation and design patterns. Projects require students to build and explain programs in both languages.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Covers software design, creation, testing and maintenance. Uses C++ and Haskell and covers planning, requirements gathering, testing, deployment and maintenance through discussions and code reviews.

coursesExamined.name: Algorithms & Data Structures
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algorithm design and analysis, emphasizing how algorithms and data structures affect execution time. Students examine sorting, searching, random-number generation, string matching and graph algorithms, then study computability, verification, reductions and complexity classes. Programming and mathematical exercises develop algorithmic understanding, while projects require students to design, execute and report experimental investigations of performance.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops algorithm design, data structures and performance analysis for computational modelling
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Teaches design and analysis of algorithms and data structures, emphasizing performance analysis and focusing on prominent algorithms and data structures.

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Algorithms
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies algebraic algorithms and advanced optimization methods through mathematical reasoning, implementation and experimental analysis. Fast and exact arithmetic, number-theoretic algorithms, matrix multiplication and Fourier transformation lead into hashing, greedy methods, dynamic programming and network flows. Laboratories develop algorithmic understanding, while projects investigate exact computing and optimization, including hypotheses, measured performance and sensitivity analysis.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops algebraic andnumber-theoretic algorithms,matrix/Fourier methods,greedy/dynamic programming andnetwork flows. Experimental projects test exact computing/optimisation,performance andsensitivity. This provides concrete algorithmic optimisation,not a complete combinatorial-optimisation sequence.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Studies modern algebraic algorithms and optimization methods. Emphasises algorithmic thinking and mathematical modelling of computational problems.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Data Science
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data. Students import, clean, transform and join data, explore patterns, and construct visualizations using tidy-data principles and the grammar of graphics. Web scraping and basic programming functions extend the workflow. A student research project applies these tools to a question using data from a field of interest.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops foundational data cleaning, visualisation and analysis through applied research projects
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation. Explores spatial and text data and includes hands‑on work with datasets from various disciplines.

coursesExamined.name: Machine Learning
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes. Students study regression and classification, model accuracy, resampling, regularization, nonlinear models, trees, support vector machines and unsupervised learning. Practical assignments evaluate methods on real data using R or Python. Projects emphasize informative predictor construction, test-set prediction, appropriate model choice and clear reporting of results and limitations.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Covers core machine learning techniques from linear regression to advanced tree‑based methods. Discusses strengths and weaknesses and applies methods to real data from fields like medicine, physics and economics.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops predictive modelling through regression, classification, resampling, tree methods and clustering
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Machine Learning introduces methods for understanding data and making predictions, including linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering. Real-world examples illustrate the methods, their strengths and limitations.

coursesExamined.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops neural-network theory and practical implementation in Python, Keras and TensorFlow. Students build and train simple networks before studying multilayer architectures, backpropagation, regularization and model evaluation. Later work applies deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects construct predictors for tabular data and investigate an independently chosen image- or text-based prediction problem, with experimental results reported in a paper.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores theory and practice of neural networks. Students build basic networks and progress to complex networks for computer vision, and discuss recent developments in large language and image generation models.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct neural-network theory and Python/TensorFlow implementation, including tabular data, computer vision and text applications, extends the computational data-science route. These broader applications are not represented as additional econometrics training.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Neural Networks & Deep Learning combines theory with practical Python, Keras and TensorFlow implementations. Students build and train networks, study backpropagation, regularisation and model evaluation, and apply deep learning to computer vision, time series and text, including transformers. Projects investigate prediction problems and report experimental results.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Programming
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python. Students develop structured programs using branching, iteration, functions and data collections, then progress to recursion, exception handling and object-oriented programming with inheritance. Elements of logic, sets and enumeration support computational reasoning. Exercises and projects require students to write, trace, test, debug and explain programs that solve problems of moderate complexity.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.

coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Introduces programming and computer science. Covers structured programming, data constructs, testing, debugging and object‑oriented programming with Python, and develops computational problem‑solving skills.

coursesExamined.name: Mathematical Methods

Functions, limits and differentiation lead to optimization, Taylor series, complex numbers, integration and differential equations. Students solve problems analytically and with Mathematica, including numerical approximation. A project implements, analyzes and adapts a dynamic model, requiring interpretation of its behaviour and explanation of the computational results.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces linear algebra (vectors, matrices, eigenvalues) and calculus (limits, differentiation, integration) to construct and solve equations. Provides problem‑solving skills applicable across disciplines.

coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Mathematical Methods develops foundational techniques in differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations. coursesExamined.name: Linear Algebra

Students study least-squares approximation, symmetric matrices, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis. Mathematica exercises teach computer-algebra approaches to larger problems alongside analytical problem-solving.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces systems of equations, vectors, matrices and linear spaces with emphasis on visual and conceptual understanding. Applies concepts across fields and includes hands‑on exercises using computer algebra software.

coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Linear Algebra studies systems of equations, matrices, vectors, linear transformations and vector spaces. Students examine eigenvalues, orthogonality, least-squares approximation, quadratic forms and singular value decomposition. Applications include discrete signals, difference equations, Markov chains, dynamical systems, graphics and principal component analysis, with Mathematica supporting analytical problem-solving.

coursesExamined.name: Computational & Numerical Methods

coursesExamined.name: Probability & Statistics

coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.

coursesExamined.name: Ethics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. Applies theories to practical issues such as animal rights, privacy, future generations, war, punishment, disability and equality.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops utilitarian,Kantian,virtue,contractarian andfeminist ethical theories,argument evaluation andindependent essays. coursesExamined.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in the medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers in other domains. In addition to technical training, the course emphasizes clear academic communication. It will equip you with the skills necessary to apply advanced statistical techniques to real-world research problems. With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.

candidateChallenge.BENGATE101: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
candidateChallenge.BENBUSI312: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
candidateChallenge.BENECON314: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.
